independent symbolic reduction of the critical radial numerator
correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the family directly. On the regular first-quadrant boundary arc, \(F_s'(e^{it})=iY_s(t)\) with \(Y_s\) strictly decreasing from \(+\infty\) to \(-\infty\), so there is one zero \(t_s\). Its zero equation is equivalent to \(\cos t_s-\sin t_s=1-2s\). Writing \(c=\cos t_s\), \(q=\sin t_s\), the radial numerator in \(\operatorname{Im}F_s'(re^{it_s})\) reduces under \(c^2+q^2=1\) to \(\tfrac12(q-c)(1+c+q)(1-r)^2\); this factorization was independently rechecked symbolically from the displayed formulas. Hence the radial integral \(\operatorname{Im}(e^{-it_s}F_s(e^{it_s}))\) has sign \(2s-1\). Since \(\operatorname{Re}(e^{it}F_s'(e^{it})/F_s(e^{it}))=Y_s(t)\operatorname{Im}(e^{-it}F_s(e^{it}))/|e^{-it}F_s(e^{it})|^2\), strict negativity occurs immediately on one side of \(t_s\) for every \(s\ne1/2\), and analyticity across that nonsingular arc moves the negative value into the disk.
